# Lumiose UI

> `@lumiose/ui`: accessible, unstyled UI primitives built on native elements (`<dialog>`, popover, invoker commands, CSS anchor positioning), server-rendered without hydration. Style them with your own CSS or the optional default theme.

These docs ship in `@lumiose/ui` and match the installed version: `node_modules/@lumiose/ui/docs`.
In a project that depends on it, `lumiose docs ui` prints the index and `lumiose docs dialog` a
component's page; the Lumiose MCP server's `ui_components` tool lists every component's parts,
props, events and styling hooks. The Lumiose docs: `node_modules/lumiose/docs/llms.txt`.

## Overview

- [UI components](README.md): `@lumiose/ui`: accessible, unstyled UI primitives built on native elements (`<dialog>`, popover, invoker commands, CSS anchor positioning), server-rendered without hydration. Style them with your own CSS or the optional default theme.
- [Installation](installation.md): Add `@lumiose/ui` to a Lumiose app and import its stylesheets, and the default theme if you want its look. The components then render in server HTML, without an island, and a page loads only the small scripts of the components it renders.
- [Theming](theming.md): `@lumiose/ui` is unstyled: its stylesheets hold only what the components need to work. The optional default theme gives them a look, light and dark, through `--lu-` custom properties you can change; or style the parts with your own CSS.

## Components

- [Accordion](accordion.md): A stack of items whose triggers show and hide their panels, after the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern: each item is a native `<details>`, one open at a time through the browser's exclusive group (`name`) or several, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript and find-in-page opens the item it lands in. `<lu-accordion>`, a 1 kB light-DOM element, adds the arrow keys and Base UI's animation hooks. `bind:value` (or `value` and `onValueChange`) keeps a signal in sync.
- [Autocomplete](autocomplete.md): A text input with suggestions, for text that may be anything (a search, a tag, an address): the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with list autocomplete, after Base UI's Autocomplete. Unlike a Combobox, the text is the value: the input has the name and submits what is typed, and choosing a suggestion only fills it in. It runs on the Combobox's element (`<lu-combobox free>`, 4.3 kB) and parts, on server-rendered pages and in islands; `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync. Filtering, inline completion, groups, an empty state and a status.
- [Avatar](avatar.md): A person's picture with a fallback, such as their initials, after Base UI's Avatar: the image loads in the server HTML and shows once it has loaded, the fallback shows until then, after an optional delay, and when the image fails. Both sit in one cell, so neither moves the other. A 0.5 kB script follows the image's loading status; without JavaScript the image covers the fallback when it loads.
- [Button](button.md): A native `<button>`, after Base UI's Button. It is `type="button"` unless you say otherwise, so it submits a form only when asked to. Disabled it leaves the tab order; with `focusableWhenDisabled` it stays focusable as `aria-disabled="true"` (a loading state keeps focus where it was) and a tiny script cancels its clicks.
- [Checkbox](checkbox.md): A native `<input type="checkbox">`, after Base UI's Checkbox: Space and a label click toggle it, the form submits its value when checked, reset and `required` work, in server HTML and without JavaScript. `indeterminate`, `readOnly`, the parent checkbox of a Checkbox Group and `bind:checked` come on top, with a 0.6 kB script shared with Radio Group and Switch.
- [Checkbox Group](checkbox-group.md): A group of checkboxes with one value, the list of the checked ones, after Base UI's CheckboxGroup: a native `<fieldset>` whose checkboxes share a name, so the form submits each checked value and a disabled group disables them all, without JavaScript. A parent checkbox checks them all and shows checked, mixed or unchecked as they are; `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.
- [Collapsible](collapsible.md): A panel that its trigger shows and hides: a native `<details>` whose `<summary>` is the trigger, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, keeps the browser's keyboard handling, and opens when find-in-page or a link lands inside it. A 0.7 kB script adds Base UI's animation hooks. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.
- [Combobox](combobox.md): A text input that filters a list of options, for picking one value or several from many: the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with list autocomplete, after Base UI's Combobox. The input shows the option's label and the form gets its value. `<lu-combobox>`, a 4.3 kB form-associated light-DOM element, runs it on server-rendered pages and in islands; `bind:value` and `bind:open` keep signals in sync. Groups, an empty state, a status, a clear button, multiple values with chips, validation and async options.
- [Context Menu](context-menu.md): A menu opened at the pointer by a right-click in its trigger area, a long press on a touch screen, or Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key: Menu's popup and items, with Menu's keys, typeahead, submenus and dismissal. A 0.6 kB script on top of Menu's (3.9 kB together) opens it; without JavaScript the browser shows its own menu. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.
- [Dialog](dialog.md): A modal dialog, or an alert dialog that needs an answer: a native `<dialog>` opened and closed by invoker commands, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, and a 0.8 kB script closes the native element's gaps where JavaScript runs. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.
- [Drawer](drawer.md): A panel that slides in from an edge of the window and that a swipe toward that edge closes: a Dialog (a native modal `<dialog>` opened by an invoker command, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript) against the edge its `swipeDirection` names. A 1 kB script adds the swipe, with the close buttons, Escape and a click on the backdrop as its alternatives. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.
- [Field](field.md): A form field: a label, a native control, a description and its errors, wired with `for`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`, after Base UI's Field. Validation is the browser's constraint validation (`required`, `type`, `pattern`, `minlength`…); a 1.1 kB script shows it in the field's Error parts at the right time, instead of the browser's bubble, and focuses the first invalid field on submit. A Form's server errors render in the HTML, so they work without JavaScript. In an island, `validate` adds checks of your own, async ones included, and `Field.Validity` renders from the field's validity.
- [Fieldset](fieldset.md): A group of related fields with a caption: a native `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, after Base UI's Fieldset. The browser names the group by its legend and disables every control inside a disabled fieldset, with no JavaScript and no CSS of its own. The legend also names a Checkbox Group or a Radio Group.
- [Form](form.md): A native `<form>` that hands its fields the server's errors, after Base UI's Form. Pass the data a form action gives `fail()` as `errors`, and each Field shows the message for its `name`, in the HTML the server renders back (no JavaScript needed) or, with `submit()`, in an island. Submission, validation and the first invalid field's focus are the platform's and Field's.
- [Input](input.md): A native `<input>`, after Base UI's Input: every type, constraint and autofill the browser has, plus `onValueChange` and `bind:value`. Inside a Field (as `Field.Control`) it takes the field's id, name and ARIA references. No script, no CSS of its own.
- [Menu](menu.md): A menu of commands, links, checkbox and radio items and submenus, opened by a button: the trigger's `popovertarget` opens it and CSS anchor positioning places it, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, and a 3.3 kB script adds the APG Menu Button keyboard contract where JavaScript runs. `bind:open`, `bind:checked` and `bind:value` keep signals in sync in islands.
- [Menubar](menubar.md): A bar of menus, such as an app's File, Edit and View, after Base UI's Menubar and the WAI-ARIA menubar pattern: `Menu.Root`s inside `<lu-menubar role="menubar">`, whose triggers are the bar's items. Menu's popups, items, submenus and dismissal; the bar is one tab stop, the arrow keys move between its items and between open menus, and once a menu is open, hovering another item opens its menu instead. A 0.6 kB script on top of Menu's (4.0 kB together); without JavaScript each trigger opens its menu.
- [Meter](meter.md): A measurement within a known range (storage used, a password's strength, a rating), after Base UI's Meter: a native `<meter>` (with its value, range and `aria-valuetext`), labelled, with the value as text (a percentage of the range by default, or your `Intl.NumberFormat` options). No script.
- [Navigation Menu](navigation-menu.md): A site's navigation whose items open panels of links, after Base UI's NavigationMenu and the WAI-ARIA disclosure navigation pattern: a `<nav>` landmark around a list, each trigger opening its content through `popovertarget` (a native popover placed under it by CSS anchor positioning), so the links work and the panels open on a click, one at a time, in server HTML with no JavaScript. A 2.1 kB script adds hover intent, the arrow keys, closing when focus leaves and the direction a panel comes in from. `bind:value` (or `value` and `onValueChange`) keeps the open item in a signal.
- [Number Field](number-field.md): A number input with buttons to step it, after Base UI's NumberField and the APG spinbutton. Without `format` it is a native `<input type="number">`, which steps, validates and submits without JavaScript; with `format` (`Intl.NumberFormat` options: a currency, a percentage, grouping) it shows the formatted number, reads what is typed back in the same locale, and a hidden input submits the number. `<lu-number-field>`'s 2.3 kB script adds Page Up and Page Down, Home and End, press-and-hold buttons, a scrub area, the wheel when asked, and commit-time clamping. `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.
- [OTP Field](otp-field.md): A one-time code input, after Base UI's OTPField: one native `<input>` shown as one slot per character. SMS autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`), paste, Backspace, the arrow keys, `maxlength`, `pattern`, `required` and the form's value are the platform's, without JavaScript too, and assistive technology meets one labelled text field. `<lu-otp-field>`'s 1.3 kB script lays the input over the slots, keeps the code to the allowed characters, and reports completion. `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.
- [Popover](popover.md): A popup anchored to its trigger: a native `popover` opened and closed by the trigger's `popovertarget`, placed with CSS anchor positioning, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript. A 2.6 kB script moves focus into it and back, dismisses it as Base UI does (not on a right-click), keeps `aria-expanded` current and places it in browsers without anchor positioning. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands. A trigger can open it on hover (`openOnHover`), and a `modal` popover is a modal `<dialog>` that makes the page behind it inert.
- [Preview Card](preview-card.md): A card that previews a link's destination while the pointer or keyboard focus rests on the link, after Base UI's PreviewCard. The trigger is the link itself, which works as a link without JavaScript; the card is a manual popover placed with Popover's placement and opened with its hover timing by a 2.2 kB script. It is hoverable, persistent and dismissible (WCAG 1.4.13). `bind:open` keeps a signal in sync.
- [Progress](progress.md): A task's progress, after Base UI's Progress: a native `<progress>` (the progress bar for assistive technology, with its value and `aria-valuetext`), labelled, with the value as text (a percentage by default, or your `Intl.NumberFormat` options). With no value it is indeterminate. No script.
- [Radio](radio-group.md): A group of radios with one value, after Base UI's RadioGroup and Radio: native radios in a `<fieldset role="radiogroup">`. The browser gives the group one tab stop, arrow keys that move and select (skipping disabled radios), `required`, submission and reset, in server HTML and without JavaScript; a legend names the group. `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.
- [Scroll Area](scroll-area.md): A scrolling region with custom scrollbars laid over native scrolling, after Base UI's ScrollArea. The viewport scrolls natively (the wheel, touch, the keyboard, find-in-page), is focusable while it overflows, and traps nothing; without JavaScript its native scrollbars show. `<lu-scroll-area>`'s 1.4 kB script hides them and draws its own, which show on hover, while scrolling and while focused, take a thumb drag and a track press, and expose the overflow as data attributes and CSS variables.
- [Select](select.md): A native `<select>` for picking one value from a list: it works with no JavaScript, submits with its form and keeps the platform's keyboard, typeahead and mobile pickers. Where the browser has customizable select (`appearance: base-select`, Chrome 135, Safari 27), `Select.Trigger` and `Select.Value` shape the button, the picker is styleable and options may hold more than text; elsewhere it is the classic select. No script; `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync in islands.
- [Separator](separator.md): A native `<hr>` between groups of content, after Base UI's Separator: announced as a separator, horizontal by default, or vertical between the items of a row with `aria-orientation="vertical"`. No script.
- [Slider](slider.md): A value picked within a range by dragging or with the keys, or a range with two thumbs, after Base UI's Slider. Each thumb is a native `<input type="range">`, so it drags, takes the arrow keys, Home and End, follows the text direction and submits with its form, in server HTML and without JavaScript. `<lu-slider>` adds Page Up and Page Down, keeps a range's thumbs in order, moves the nearest thumb on a press on the track and keeps the value text current. `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.
- [Switch](switch.md): On or off, for a setting: a native `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`, after Base UI's Switch. Space and a label click toggle it, the form submits its value when on, `required` and reset work, in server HTML and without JavaScript, and assistive technology announces a switch. `bind:checked` keeps a signal in sync.
- [Tabs](tabs.md): A tab list and the panel of the selected tab, after the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: the server HTML holds the whole state (roles, `aria-selected`, the roving tab stop, the hidden panels), and `<lu-tabs>`, a 1.2 kB light-DOM element, adds the arrow keys and the selection. Manual or automatic activation, horizontal or vertical, right-to-left aware, with an optional indicator that slides to the selected tab; `bind:value` (or `value` and `onValueChange`) keeps a signal in sync.
- [Toast](toast.md): Short notices in a region of their own, after Base UI's toast: server HTML renders them (a form action's result), and islands add, update and close them through a toast manager. `<lu-toast-viewport>`, a 2.3 kB light-DOM element, puts them in the top layer, times them (pausing on hover and focus), limits how many show, closes them on a swipe, Escape or their close button, focuses the region on F6, and makes screen readers announce them.
- [Toggle](toggle.md): A two-state button (bold, mute, pin), after Base UI's Toggle: a native `<button type="button" aria-pressed>`. Its label stays the same; `aria-pressed` tells pressed from not. On its own the component presses it, in an island, and `bind:pressed` keeps a signal in sync; inside a Toggle Group the group presses it, on server pages too.
- [Toggle Group](toggle-group.md): A set of Toggles with one value, after Base UI's ToggleGroup: text alignment (one pressed at a time) or text style (several). `<lu-toggle-group role="group">` presses its toggles and gives the group one tab stop that the arrow keys, Home and End move, following the orientation and the direction, on server pages and in islands. `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.
- [Toolbar](toolbar.md): A set of controls with one tab stop, after Base UI's Toolbar and the APG toolbar pattern: `<lu-toolbar role="toolbar">` moves focus between its items with the arrow keys, Home and End, following the orientation and the text direction. Its items are native: buttons that stay focusable when disabled, links, inputs, and the toggles of a Toggle Group inside it. The server HTML has the single tab stop already; a 0.9 kB script moves it.
- [Tooltip](tooltip.md): A short tip next to its trigger, on hover or keyboard focus: a native `popover="hint"` with `role="tooltip"`, placed with CSS anchor positioning. The trigger is described by the tip in server HTML, so screen readers announce it without hovering; a 1.5 kB script opens and closes it as Base UI's tooltip does. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.
